title: devbin writes the operator's home directory into every estate's tracked manifest, and five of those estates are public
body:
Found in Cdsync on 2026-09-15, while vendoring devbin 0.1.1 into a public repository. Read from this repository's `lib/install` and the vendored `bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet` and `lib/cmd/upgrade`, and measured across every sibling estate under the same parent directory. The home directory is written `<home>` below; the manifests carry it literally.

`lib/install:526` writes the source root into the manifest header as an absolute path:

    printf '# source: %s\n' "$srcroot"

so every `devbin install --into` and every `devbin upgrade` leaves `bin/.devbin/manifest.sha256` carrying a line of the form `# source: <home>/<path to the devbin install>`.

**The manifest is a tracked file in twelve of the thirteen estates that carry one**, and each of those twelve holds the line. **Five of them push to a public GitHub repository**: Intent, MicroGPTEx, Molt, Riffle and Utilz. So each of those publishes the operator's home directory, and with it their login name, and the next upgrade rewrites the line even after someone scrubs it by hand. Cdsync is the thirteenth and the only one that does not track the file: it gitignores the manifest and pins that with a test, which is a workaround and costs it the manifest's own purpose -- a clone cannot tell that an edited vendored file was edited.

## Why

The line is not decoration, so dropping it is not the fix. Two readers depend on it:

- `lib/cmd/upgrade:193` reads it through `manifest_source` as the default `--from`, and dies with `no source recorded` when it is absent.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:229` (`recorded_source`) reads it, and `fleet` compares it byte-for-byte with the install prefix (`[ "$src" = "$prefix" ]`, around `:348`) to decide between `level`, `upgrade` and `upgrade + repoint`.

`fleet`'s own `scan` already renders roots as `${root#"$HOME"/}`, so the display side of devbin already treats the home prefix as something not to print; only the recording side writes it down.

## Why it is worth an issue

Several of these estates carry a rule that no absolute path belongs in a tracked file, because the repository is public. devbin is the one writer that breaks that rule on every run, in every estate at once, and a scrub does not survive the next upgrade. The five public repositories already carry the line in their history, so a fix stops the next write; it does not remove what has been pushed.

## Shape of a fix, not a ruling

Record the source relative to the home directory when it lies under it -- `# source: ~/<path>` -- and expand `~` in the one reader both call sites could share, so `upgrade`'s default `--from` and `fleet`'s repoint comparison see the same absolute path they see today. A source outside the home directory has no username in it to leak and can stay absolute. Hold it with an arm per reader: an install whose source is under the home directory writes no home path and still upgrades with no `--from`, and `fleet` still reports `level` for an estate whose recorded source is the current prefix, whichever form it was recorded in. Existing manifests keep the absolute form until their next upgrade, so a reader has to accept both.
